name: Cincinnati Northern Kentucky International Airport
before:
The airport for Cincinnati, though it is not in Ohio. It sits in Boone County, Kentucky, near Hebron, and serves the whole tri-state area. The code comes from Covington, the nearest city when the airport opened.

Passengers get one terminal with two concourses and 51 gates between them. Both concourses are islands, reached only by an underground moving walkway and a people mover, so allow a little longer than the terminal map suggests. International arrivals without pre-clearance are handled in Concourse B.

There are nonstop flights to more than fifty destinations across North America and Europe, but the real volume here is freight. This is a global cargo hub for Amazon Air, DHL Aviation, Atlas Air, ABX Air and Kalitta Air, fifth busiest in the United States for cargo and twelfth in the world.

Worth a look while waiting: five of the Art Deco mosaic murals made in 1932 for Cincinnati Union Terminal, by Winold Reiss, were saved from demolition and are on show here.
after:
The airport for Cincinnati, though it is not in Ohio. It sits near Hebron in Boone County, Kentucky, serving the whole tri-state area.

Passengers get one terminal with two concourses, A and B. Both are reached only through an underground tunnel, by train, moving walkway or on foot, so allow a little longer than the terminal map suggests. International arrivals without pre-clearance are handled in Concourse B.

The airport says it offers more than 55 nonstop destinations across North America and Europe, but the real volume here is freight. It is Amazon's main US air hub and a DHL hub, and in 2025 it was the fifth busiest cargo airport in the United States.

Worth a look while waiting: five of the mosaic murals Winold Reiss made for Cincinnati Union Terminal in the early 1930s came here in the 1970s and are on show in the main terminal.

claims.claim: the code comes from Covington, the nearest city when the airport opened
claims.wasBefore: The code comes from Covington, the nearest city when the airport opened.
claims.why: Only Wikipedia states where the code comes from. The FAA's master record still names Covington as the airport's associated city, which fits but does not say it; the operator's pages, Cincinnati Magazine's piece on the airport and the Kenton County Airport Board page do not explain the code, and the operator's 2022 anniversary release is gone (404).

claims.claim: 51 gates
claims.wasBefore: Passengers get one terminal with two concourses and 51 gates between them.
claims.why: Sources disagree. Wikipedia gives 51 (23 in A, 28 in B); the operator's own directions name gates A-4 to A-23 and B-1 to B-28, which make 48. The terminal and the two concourses are kept.

claims.claim: concourses are islands, reached by an underground moving walkway and a people mover
claims.wasBefore: Both concourses are islands, reached only by an underground moving walkway and a people mover
claims.why: Reworded in the operator's terms (tunnel, trains, moving walkways, walking); see the kept claim.

claims.why: Replaced by the airport's own current count, attributed ('more than 55'), as the brief asks for destination counts.

claims.claim: global cargo hub for Atlas Air, ABX Air and Kalitta Air
claims.wasBefore: This is a global cargo hub for Amazon Air, DHL Aviation, Atlas Air, ABX Air and Kalitta Air
claims.why: Atlas Air, ABX Air and Kalitta Air rest on Wikipedia alone; the operator names only Amazon and DHL as hubs, with a presence by FedEx. Amazon and DHL are kept.

claims.claim: twelfth in the world for cargo
claims.why: The operator's own '12th largest globally' is marked 2023, more than 12 months old, and its cargo has fallen since (1,869,694 tons in 2024, 1,703,828 in 2025, Spectrum News; FAA landed weight down 12.7 per cent in 2025). No current world ranking was found, so only the FAA's 2025 US rank is given.

claims.claim: Art Deco, made in 1932, saved from demolition
claims.wasBefore: five of the Art Deco mosaic murals made in 1932 for Cincinnati Union Terminal, by Winold Reiss, were saved from demolition and are on show here
claims.why: 'Art Deco' and 'saved from demolition' rest on Wikipedia alone (the operator and Cincinnati Museum Center do not use either; the Cincinnati Enquirer's 2015 article refused both grab.mjs (403) and grabb.mjs (405)). The date is widened to the early 1930s because the operator gives 1931 to 1932. The murals themselves are kept.

claims.claim: British Airways flies nonstop to London Heathrow
claims.why: Held back: verified, but a new fact that replaces nothing (the old text says only 'Europe'). For Andy: British Airways flies CVG to London Heathrow nonstop, six a week from 29 March 2026 through October 2026 on BA's own figures (Fox19, 17 November 2025); the operator's route map lists London/Heathrow and BA sells London to Cincinnati with a flight time of 8 hours 40 minutes for every month to February 2027. It matters to a UK agent, so it may be worth adding.

quote: Starting in Spring 2026, the airline will offer six weekly nonstop flights between CVG and London Heathrow Airport.
